chunks: The scholars are trustees, the pious are fortresses, and the successors are chiefs.
And in another narration: The scholars are beacons, the pious are fortresses, and the successors are chiefs.

key_terms.أُمَنَاءُ: Trustees, custodians — those entrusted with knowledge and its proper transmission
key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءُ: Successors, those appointed by bequest — specifically refers to the Imams in Shia tradition
key_terms.حُصُونٌ: Fortresses, strongholds — protective bulwarks of faith and community
key_terms.سَادَةٌ: Chiefs, masters, leaders — those of high rank and authority

ai.seo_question: What are the roles of scholars, the pious, and successors according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the three pillars of the believing community through two complementary formulations: scholars as trustees (or beacons), the pious as protective fortresses, and the Imams (successors/awsiya') as rightful chiefs. The hadith preserves both versions, acknowledging textual variation while maintaining consistency in the central message about the social and spiritual roles of these three groups. This teaching was addressed to early Shia Muslims who needed clarity on legitimate religious authority and its different dimensions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ismail Bin Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The scholars are the trustees, and the pious are the fortresses, and the successors<sup>asws</sup> are the chiefs’.

And in another report, ‘(He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said): ‘The scholars are minarets, and the pious are fortresses, and the successors<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> are the chiefs’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ’Isma‘il ibn Jabir from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “The scholars are trust worthy people, The pious ones are the strongholds and the successors (of the holy Prophet (s.a.) are the leaders.”
In another Hadith it is said, “The scholars are the light houses, the pious people are the strongholds and the successors are the leaders.”
